title: Homogeneous Equations & Rank of a Matrix
subtitle: Rank tells you how many independent equations a system actually has. Three methods exist to find it: determinant, linear dependence, and row reduction. The notes ask you to use all three on the same matrix. Homogeneous systems (all RHS = 0) always have x = 0 as a solution — the real question is whether others exist.
learningOutcome: Rank tells you how many independent equations a system actually has. Three methods exist to find it: determinant, linear dependence, and row reduction. The notes ask you to use all three on the same matrix. Homogeneous systems (all RHS = 0) always have x = 0 as a solution — the real question is whether others exist.

content.text: Homogeneous: all RHS constants = 0, written AX = 0. x = 0 always satisfies it (trivial solution). Non-trivial solutions exist only when det(A) = 0. Non-homogeneous: at least one RHS ≠ 0. No guarantee of any solution.

Key Distinction
AX = 0
Always has x = 0. Non-trivial solutions exist only if rank(A) < n (equivalently: det(A) = 0).
AX = b (b≠0)
Solution exists only if rank(A) = rank([A|b]). x = 0 is NOT a solution unless b happens to be 0.

Common mistake — "The homogeneous system has no solution." Wrong. AX = 0 always has x = 0. What you mean is: "the only solution is the trivial solution x = 0." These are different and examiners penalise the incorrect phrasing.

topics.title: Three Methods for Rank — Applied to the Same Matrix

subtopics.title: Three Methods for Rank — Applied to the Same Matrix

content.text: We'll use A = [[2,4,6],[1,3,5],[9,10,11]] from the class notes and apply all three methods. All three must give the same answer.
Take top-left 2×2: [ 2 4 ] [ 1 3 ] det = (2×3) - (4×1) = 6 - 4 = 2 ≠ 0 Non-zero 2×2 found → Rank exists at order 2
Swap R₁ and R₂ to get 1 as the leading entry
Non-zero rows: Row 1 and Row 2 → count = 2 Zero rows: Row 3 → count = 1
If an exam asks for all three methods, row reduction is the most reliable. Always count the number of non-zero rows after reducing, not the total number of rows.
